newsitem.title: UK: Halliburton agrees 72.6 mln stg bid for OGC.
newsitem.headline: Halliburton agrees 72.6 mln stg bid for OGC.

text.p: Halliburton Co, the U.S. energy engineering group, said on Tuesday it had agreed terms for a takeover bid with Scottish-based oilfield engineering services company OGC International Plc that values OGC at about 72.6 million stg.
The offer will be at 119.3 pence cash per OGC share, Halliburton said in a statement.

OGC announced on December 21 that it had received an approach from Halliburton. On the previous day, its shares had traded at 75p, giving the agreed offer a premium of about 59 percent over this price.

Halliburton said it had already received irrevocable undertakings to accept the bid from directors and interests of the Norwegian Fred Olsen shipping and offshore group, which together represent about 40.3 percent of the firm's issued share capital.

One result of the acquisition would be to give Halliburton full control of Brown & Root AOC, currently a joint venture between Halliburton's Brown & Root unit and AOC, OGC's principal operating subsidiary.
The U.S. group said this would give it "a leading position in the UK market for integrated oil and and gas production services".
